body:
Copying what I said on my [PR](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/10954#issuecomment-2807332020).

I personally think `requestClose()` should just be specced and implemented differently. 

```
1. If this does not have an open attribute, then return.
2. Let canceled be the result of firing an event named cancel at this, with the cancelable attribute initialized to true.
3. If canceled is false, close the dialog this with returnValue.
```

We could also then drop dialog's enable close watcher for requestClose() and request close return value.

This doesn't fully get rid of the close watcher getEnabledStatus but that's actually a product of closedby rather than requestClose()

Regarding my previous point there's two discrepencies with what is currently specced.

https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#close-watcher-request-close - step 5 means non fully active documents early return, but I don't think this is actually needed.

10.2 also consumes user action history activation and I again don't think that's actually needed in this case (nor when CloseWatcher.requestClose() is called manually, they both "bypass" the protections)

After some discussions with Keith I think we've come up with a solution, it leaves most of the current stuff intact and only changes my PR to behave slightly differently which should address all issues.

It does go with the approach of doing less connected checks which might not be desirable per some discussion in whatnot but we can discuss that further.

The problems (at least in Chromium) all seem to simply stem from a few **missing** connected/active checks. (See CL [here](https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/6476484).) Those have equivalent fixes in the spec. E.g. the `dialog.requestClose()` [algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interactive-elements.html#dom-dialog-requestclose) currently just early-outs if the dialog doesn't have an `open` attribute. But it should likely also early-out unless the dialog is connected and the document is active. Perhaps adding *more* checks is a better solution than *fewer* checks?

@mfreed7 one concern raised with this is that it means `requestClose` behaves differently to `close` in ways which are mostly accidental. It creates a somewhat incoherent API: some methods throw in some situations, others silently fail, others run and dispatch events regardless.

Iirc I also think we ran into situations where this could result in a broken dialog. Related to setting open to true, inserting into a disconnected element and then connecting that element to the document. Where none of the setup steps would run. (Can't remember specifics perhaps Keith remembers better)

I'll reiterate my position from WHATNOT, which is sympathetic to @mfreed7's. `requestClose()` is meant to imitate a user closing the dialog, and using it when the dialog is not connected doesn't really make sense.

I agree the dialog API is already incoherent in how it handles disconnected dialogs:

- `show()` doesn't care
- `showModal()` throws (we changed this in https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/10705)
- `close()` doesn't care
- `requestClose()` doesn't care right now

I would prefer it if they all threw. I think we should have extended https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/10705 to cover all the dialog methods (and all popover methods!)

Fwiw we can add connected checks to requestClose if we want to,  personally I don't think we should but that's a strong opinion weakly held. I've already been convinced that actually requestClose can still make use of close watcher infra and that it does indeed provide a benefit.

The main issue is whether other algorithms such as dialog insertion, removal and attribute change steps do or don't check for connectedness.

I've not verified with an implementation yet but I think the result we (Me and Keith) came to on my PR is what we need for those algorithms. Else there's various combinations of weird things you can still end up doing.

> I'll reiterate my position from WHATNOT, which is sympathetic to [@mfreed7](https://github.com/mfreed7)'s. `requestClose()` is meant to imitate a user closing the dialog, and using it when the dialog is not connected doesn't really make sense.
> 
> I agree the dialog API is already incoherent in how it handles disconnected dialogs:
> 
> * `show()` doesn't care
> * `showModal()` throws (we changed this in [Guard showModal() and showPopover() with fully active checks #10705](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/10705))
> * `close()` doesn't care
> * `requestClose()` doesn't care right now
> 
> I would prefer it if they all threw. I think we should have extended [#10705](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/10705) to cover all the dialog methods (and all popover methods!)

I think (modulo compat issues) I'm supportive of making `show()` throw in the same way we made `showModal()`. However, the non-throwing behavior of `close()` and `requestClose()` feels nice from a developer point of view. E.g. it's nice to be able to call `close()` just to be sure, without having to `try/catch` it. Same for `requestClose()`. If the dialog isn't in a state to be showing anyway, then I'm not sure why we need to throw when close is requested. As long as the end-state is a closed dialog, shouldn't that be good? Certainly if there's a case where a *showing* dialog could be left open after a call to `{request}close()`, then that should throw, but I'm not sure there's such a case.

> Iirc I also think we ran into situations where this could result in a broken dialog. Related to setting open to true, inserting into a disconnected element and then connecting that element to the document. Where none of the setup steps would run. (Can't remember specifics perhaps Keith remembers better)

This would be good to confirm - do you have a repro? My hope would be that our existing insertion steps catch this case and run the setup steps.

> I think (modulo compat issues) I'm supportive of making `show()` throw in the same way we made `showModal()`. However, the non-throwing behavior of `close()` and `requestClose()` feels nice from a developer point of view. E.g. it's nice to be able to call `close()` just to be sure, without having to `try/catch` it. Same for `requestClose()`. If the dialog isn't in a state to be showing anyway, then I'm not sure why we need to throw when close is requested. As long as the end-state is a closed dialog, shouldn't that be good?

I'm open to diverging show/showModal vs. close/requestClose. But I want to double-check that we're both talking about the same scenario. This is for disconnected dialogs, right? When would you close them?

>  This is for disconnected dialogs, right? When would you close them?

One example could be feature detection. We recently added toggle events to dialog. If I want to feature detect that I could just spawn a dialog, call `show()` (or set open to true) and then call `close()`. Never connecting it to the document. If we made changes to connectedness checks that kind of code would break (not fatal because it'll have a fallback presumably?).

> > This is for disconnected dialogs, right? When would you close them?
> 
> One example could be feature detection. We recently added toggle events to dialog. If I want to feature detect that I could just spawn a dialog, call `show()` (or set open to true) and then call `close()`. Never connecting it to the document. If we made changes to connectedness checks that kind of code would break (not fatal because it'll have a fallback presumably?).

In fact this is literally what happens in the polyfill I authored: https://github.com/keithamus/dialog-toggle-events-polyfill/blob/main/polyfill.js#L2-L12. We could connect the dialog, but it gets a bit weird as that does a ton of stuff such as dispatching MutationObservers, making it more difficult to integrate code like this. Not that I think that is a _significant_ reason to avoid this, but there is definitely code in-the-wild following this pattern.

> > Iirc I also think we ran into situations where this could result in a broken dialog. Related to setting open to true, inserting into a disconnected element and then connecting that element to the document. Where none of the setup steps would run. (Can't remember specifics perhaps Keith remembers better)

> This would be good to confirm - do you have a repro? My hope would be that our existing insertion steps catch this case and run the setup steps.

Turns out this was based on a faulty assumption on my end, at least in terms of chromium implementation the insertion steps *do* run the second time. I'm not sure if the same is true in the spec but i'm guessing yes?

In which case it might come down to the question of whether requestClose() needs to work on disconnected dialogs. If it does then my PR is correct wrt connected checks, but perhaps needs active checks (modulo any mistakes), if we decide we can block it with an early return or throw then we can change it to add connected checks all over the place.

> > I think (modulo compat issues) I'm supportive of making `show()` throw in the same way we made `showModal()`. However, the non-throwing behavior of `close()` and `requestClose()` feels nice from a developer point of view. E.g. it's nice to be able to call `close()` just to be sure, without having to `try/catch` it. Same for `requestClose()`. If the dialog isn't in a state to be showing anyway, then I'm not sure why we need to throw when close is requested. As long as the end-state is a closed dialog, shouldn't that be good?
> 
> I'm open to diverging show/showModal vs. close/requestClose. But I want to double-check that we're both talking about the same scenario. This is for disconnected dialogs, right?

Correct (at least in my mind) - this is about disconnected dialogs or connected dialogs in inactive documents.

> When would you close them?

If they're actually open (connected to active document) then the new logic in https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/10954 (suitably modified to account for this issue) should close them when they're disconnected.

> Turns out this was based on a faulty assumption on my end, at least in terms of chromium implementation the insertion steps _do_ run the second time. I'm not sure if the same is true in the spec but i'm guessing yes?

Great! I think so, but it'd be good to verify.

> In which case it might come down to the question of whether requestClose() needs to work on disconnected dialogs. If it does then my PR is correct wrt connected checks, but perhaps needs active checks (modulo any mistakes), if we decide we can block it with an early return or throw then we can change it to add connected checks all over the place.

I don't think it's all over the place. In my Chromium CL it's just a handful, and since I was fixing a crash, I probably went a bit overboard on checks just in case.
Well all over the place = inserted, remove, attribute change steps + requestClose I guess?

Early return sounds reasonable to me. It's the same kind of "don't do this" signal, just with less potential compat impact.

I guess the plan is to only modify request close, and leave show() and close() to continue working on disconnected dialogs? I think that's unfortunate but I understand that practically we have some polyfills and feature testing code that are using disconnected dialogs this way, so oh well.

It's a bit unclear if we can still change those. And `details` has similar broken behavior. Let's not copy that design to any new features though.

My main takeaway from the meeting is that it's desirable to not have a CloseWatcher for a disconnected dialog. And then several things follow from that. Thinking about it now, we should make sure that the CloseWatcher does not become eligible for GC when you merely move the dialog. And test that.

To clarify when you say "move" do you mean atomic move, or remove and reinsert?

If it's remove and reinsert then I think given we don't want close watchers on disconnected dialogs then we'd destroy it when removed and recreate it when you reinsert.
Yes, remove and reinsert should recreate, as we do with browsing contexts. (I don't think I'm going to call it atomic move, it's called move in the DOM.)
Oh I think this can be closed now, as https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/11326 has been merged. If anyone disagrees we can re-open or raise a new issue with specific problems.
